subject: Audit log export, evidence & retention process — RFP EG-2027
messages:
From: Jordan Sullivan <j.sullivan@evergreenbank.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@evergreenbank.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log export + evidence request for RFP EG-2027

Chloe —

As part of Evergreen Bank's RFP (EG-2027) we have some specific questions about audit logging, retention, and exportability. Please see the attached excerpt from section 5 of the RFP for context (EG-RFP-section5.pdf). High-level asks below — can you confirm capabilities and point us to any operational runbooks / examples?

1) Retention windows: what are default retention windows for hosted logs (audit events, access logs, admin actions) and what configurable options are available for enterprise customers (e.g., 7 years / legal hold)?
2) Exportability: can you produce full audit-bundles on demand (bulk export) including event payloads, request/response metadata, timestamps, and any applicable KV cache traces? Preferred delivery: encrypted S3 export or secure scp. Typical SLA target we need: delivery within 72 hours of request.
3) Tamper evidence: describe how exports demonstrate immutability (signed manifests, checksums, timestamping). Are signed manifests available? Can you provide sample manifest schema?
4) Redaction & PII handling: what options do you offer for redaction during export (redact sensitive token content, pseudonymize user ids) vs. exporting raw data for forensic teams?
5) Chain-of-custody / legal hold: can Redwood produce chain-of-custody docs and maintain verification hashes for a customer-specified retention window?

Please reply with a short summary and attach any sample manifests or SOPs we can use in our evaluation. If helpful we can schedule a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Jordan Sullivan
Evergreen Bank — InfoSec

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I've attached a short export playbook draft for your review (redwood-export-playbook-draft.pdf). Happy to jump on a 30-min call — propose Wed 6/30 11:00am PT if that works.

Summary answers
- Retention: Hosted default retention for audit and access logs is 90 days. For Dedicated / Private deployments we support custom retention policies up to customer-requested durations (multi-year) through contract Addendum; we also offer legal-hold flags that prevent purging.
- Exportability: We can produce on-demand bulk exports containing event records, metadata, and payloads where retention policy permits. Export formats: NDJSON (primary), gzipped CSV for sampled exports, and tar.gz bundles with a top-level manifest. Delivery: encrypted S3 upload (preferred), direct SFTP, or signed HTTPS download link.
- Tamper evidence: Each export bundle includes a manifest.json with per-file SHA256 checksums and a bundle-level SHA256; manifests are signed by Redwood's export service (ECDSA) and timestamped. We can provide sample manifests.
- Redaction: Two modes — (1) Forensic/raw: export raw events (including request body) into the bundle; (2) Redacted: automated policy-driven redaction (PII masking, token replacement) applied at export time. Both modes preserved in the playbook.
- Chain-of-custody: We generate a chain-of-custody PDF that logs the export requestor, job-id, timestamps, checksums, signing certificate fingerprint, and delivery targets. We retain signed manifests and verification hashes for a configurable retention window; default retention for verification artifacts is 12 months for hosted customers, extendable under contract.

Attachments: redwood-export-playbook-draft.pdf (draft), sample manifest included in full SOP.

Next steps: please confirm the export SLA target you expect and whether you require WORM (write-once) delivery or Redwood-signed snapshots only. If you want sample evidence we can produce a sanitized export for your legal team.

Regards,

Jordan — following up with operational detail and an example runbook. See inline answers and attached stubs (evidence-sample-manifest.json, export-sop.md).

Operational export workflow (summary)
1) Request intake: customer opens an export request via Console or API (createExportJob). Job is assigned job-id and enters Pending.
2) Snapshot phase: service generates a point-in-time snapshot of the audit store and writes a compressed archive (tar.gz) to an internal staging bucket. Snapshot includes metadata index + event files (NDJSON).
3) Signing & manifest: service computes SHA256 for each file, then computes a bundle-level SHA256. The manifest.json contains per-file checksums, job-id, start/end timestamps (ISO8601 with TZ), retention-policy-id, and signingCertificateFingerprint. The manifest is ECDSA-signed using Redwood's export-signing key and timestamped via our internal timestamping authority.
4) Verification artifacts: we produce chain-of-custody.pdf (human-readable) and manifest.sig (binary signature). We retain verification artifacts in encrypted storage for the agreed verification retention period.
5) Delivery: customer-selected delivery — S3 (preferred) with bucket-owner enforced, SFTP, or HTTPS. For S3 delivery we can optionally perform server-side copy to a customer pre-provisioned bucket and apply customer KMS keys.

SLA & WORM
- SLA: For Hosted customers we offer a 72-hour best-effort window by default. We can contractually commit a 72-hour SLA for export delivery as part of Dedicated/Enterprise agreements (deal-dependent).
- WORM: Redwood does not currently provide physical WORM on hosted buckets, but we provide logical WORM via signed manifests + notarized timestamping. For customers requiring certified WORM we recommend Dedicated/Private deployments with customer-controlled storage or on-prem snapshot export which can be written to a WORM-capable appliance under customer control.

Manifest example fields (excerpt)
- job_id, file_name, file_sha256, record_count, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, redaction_mode, signed_by, signature_fingerprint

Redaction & bodies
- By default hosted exports exclude sensitive request bodies unless explicitly requested by an authorized legal/forensics contact (approval workflow). We support scoped-forensics exports for a defined query window where bodies are included and tracked in the manifest with request_body_present=true.

Retention of verification hashes
- Default: 12 months for hosted verification artifacts. Extension to 3 years or longer is supported under contract for Dedicated/Private customers; we will include retention SLA in contract schedule.

Attachments (stubs)
- evidence-sample-manifest.json (sample manifest with sanitized entries)
- export-sop.md (runbook with step-by-step operator actions)

Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD9X_export-playbook (playbook draft)

If you want a sanitized sample run now, we can turn one around within 24 hours and include signed manifest. Let me know the sample scope (time window and whether to include bodies).
